1.question: What sparked the unusual excitement about religion where young Joseph lived (v. 5)?
options: A revival among the sects, starting with the Methodists
A land dispute between two neighboring congregations that grew bitter
The arrival of a famous traveling preacher who drew great crowds
A prolonged drought that many blamed on the sins of the people

1.question: Amid the war of words, what question did Joseph keep asking himself (v. 10)?
options: Should I remain in Manchester or move to a new region?
Who of all these parties is right, or are they all wrong?
Which of these churches should I choose to please my beloved parents?
What sign would God send to show which sect was true?

1.title: A verse that changed history
1.text: In verse 11 Joseph reads James 1:5 — 'If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God' — and says no passage ever came with more power to his heart. That single verse sent him to the grove to pray.

1.question: As Joseph began to pray, what happened before he was delivered (vv. 14-15)?
options: An unseen power robbed him of his sight and strength
A violent trembling seized his whole body and all his limbs
Thick darkness seized him and bound his tongue
A chorus of mocking laughter echoed all around him

1.title: The First Vision
1.text: Verses 16-17 record the heart of the account: two Personages appeared, and one, pointing to the other, said, 'This is My Beloved Son. Hear Him!' Joseph then asked which church he should join.

1.question: How did the Methodist preacher react when Joseph told him of the vision (v. 21)?
options: He fell silent, promising to think further on the matter
He treated it with great contempt, saying it was all of the devil
He gathered the other ministers to debate the meaning of the vision
He mildly rebuked him, but asked to hear more details

1.question: By the end of the First Vision episode, what had Joseph found to be true (v. 26)?
options: The testimony of Paul — that faith comes by hearing the word of God
The testimony of James — that one who lacks wisdom may ask of God
The testimony of John — that knowing the truth would make every man free
The testimony of Isaiah — that the blind would see and the deaf would hear

1.question: How did Joseph describe the messenger who appeared at his bedside (vv. 30-31)?
options: In a tattered cloak of deep gray, his person weary, his countenance full of deep sorrow and pain
In a loose robe of exquisite whiteness, his person glorious, his countenance like lightning
In shining golden armor, his person massive, his countenance stern as a soldier
In a dark hooded mantle, his person shadowed, his countenance hidden from every view

1.title: Moroni's night visits
1.text: On the night of September 21, 1823, an angel appeared three times, each time repeating the same message. He named himself Moroni and said God had a work for Joseph to do (v. 33).

1.question: What did the messenger say was written upon gold plates (v. 34)?
options: A record of the kings of Israel and a complete guide for building sacred temples
An account of the former inhabitants of this continent and the fulness of the Gospel
A collection of psalms and sacred proverbs written by the ancient prophets of Israel and Judah
A detailed chronicle of wars between distant nations across the great sea

1.question: Quoting the prophecy of Elijah, the messenger said the hearts of the children would turn to whom (v. 39)?
options: Their kings
Their fathers
Their teachers
The prophets

1.question: After the messenger finished speaking, how did he leave the room (v. 43)?
options: He vanished in a flash of blinding light before him
He ascended through a conduit opened into heaven
He sank slowly through the floor and disappeared from sight
He turned into a bright cloud that drifted out the window

1.question: On the third visit, what did the messenger warn Satan would tempt Joseph to do (v. 46)?
options: To sell the plates to the highest bidder in town
To get the plates in order to get rich
To destroy the plates out of fear of the townspeople
To show the plates publicly before the appointed time

1.question: When Joseph told his father about the vision, what did his father reply (v. 50)?
options: That it was of God, and to do as commanded
That he must have imagined it after a long day of work
That he should tell no one until he was much older
That he should ask the local minister to interpret it

1.template: there indeed did I behold the plates, the {0}, and the breastplate

1.question: The messenger forbade Joseph from taking the plates then; how often was he to return to the place (v. 54)?
options: Twice a year, once in the spring and once in the autumn
Once, precisely one year later, and each year after
Every seven years, until the plates were finally given to him
Three times, before receiving final permission to take them

1.question: Where did Joseph find the plates deposited (vv. 51-52)?
options: Under a large fallen tree, in a wooden chest, in a valley near Palmyra
Under a stone of considerable size, in a stone box on a hill near Manchester
Under a great boulder beside a stream, in a leather pouch, on a hill near Fayette
In the loft of his father's house, inside an iron trunk, on a property near Colesville

1.question: What common story arose from Joseph working for Josiah Stoal (v. 56)?
options: That he had found buried Spanish treasure
That he had been a money-digger
That he had learned magic from a traveling stranger
That he secretly worked for a wealthy farmer

1.question: On what date did the messenger finally deliver the plates to Joseph (v. 59)?
options: September 21, 1823
December 23, 1805
September 22, 1827

1.question: Who tore up the certificate, saying there was no such thing as the ministering of angels (v. 65)?
options: Professor Samuel Kingsley
Professor Charles Anthon
Reverend Ezra Thompson
The renowned professor Nathaniel Webster

1.title: Restoration of the Priesthood
1.text: In May 1829, while translating, Joseph and Oliver Cowdery prayed about baptism. A heavenly messenger — John the Baptist — laid hands on them and conferred the Aaronic Priesthood (vv. 68-69).
